testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If you must drive very slowly, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn drivers behind you that you are driving slowly. Check your local laws first to make sure this is allowed.

questions.question: What two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear?

options.text: Oil pressure and air brake pressure.

questions.explanation: Check your vehicle manual for the correct engine speed (rpm) range. Shift up when you reach the top of that range. Also watch your speedometer for road speed (mph) and shift up as needed for each gear.

questions.question: How should you apply the brake pedal when stopping?
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly. This helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What is one way to deal with blind spots?

options.text: Drive faster than other vehicles so they cannot pass you.
Drive in the left lane so you only need to watch vehicles on your right.
Check your mirrors often and watch where other vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors often and watch where other vehicles are.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly to see traffic around you. This helps you spot vehicles that may be in your blind spots.

questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, how does this affect your braking distance?
questions.explanation: When you double your speed, your braking distance multiplies by four. Doubling speed from 20 to 40 mph makes your vehicle need four times as much distance to stop.

questions.question: During an inspection, brake pads should be:
questions.explanation: Brake pads and shoes must not have oil, grease, or brake fluid on them during an inspection.

questions.question: During a driving skills test, if you must stop before making a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Stop after the stop line to see better.
Keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: Stop smoothly behind any stop line or stop sign. Keep your front wheels straight and do not let your vehicle roll. If there is a vehicle ahead, stop where you can still see its rear tires.

questions.question: What is a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle as set by the manufacturer
The rating of a combination vehicle per axle

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle as set by the manufacturer
questions.explanation: GVWR is the maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to affect your body?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your muscles, reaction time, vision, and judgment. Some people feel the effects after just one drink. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What is one way to prevent hydroplaning on wet roads?

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread depth.
Let air out of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your tires have good tread depth.
questions.explanation: Worn tire tread or low tire pressure increases the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads. Keep your tires properly inflated and replace them when tread is worn.

questions.question: What is one way to avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.explanation: Plan ahead and allow extra time for your trip. This helps prevent frustration that can lead to aggressive driving. Other ways to avoid aggressive driving include driving at a safe speed, keeping a safe distance from other cars, and not making rude gestures.

questions.question: If you stop on a one-way or divided highway, how far behind your vehicle should you place warning devices?
questions.explanation: Place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind your vehicle on a one-way or divided highway.

questions.question: When should placards be used?

options.text: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
When there is extra space on a truck.
Only when hazardous materials weigh more than 200 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Use warning placards whenever a vehicle carries hazardous materials. Display placards on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of bad brake drums or shoes?

options.text: Shoes not covered in brake fluid

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes not covered in brake fluid
questions.explanation: Signs of brake problems include cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are worn too thin or broken. Shoes should NOT have brake fluid on them.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off within a few seconds.
Stay on until you turn them off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should stop right away after you start the engine. If they stay on, there is a problem with your vehicle.

questions.question: Cargo in a trailer should:

options.text: Be stacked no higher than three feet.
Be secured to prevent movement during transport.
Have heavy items placed on top of light items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be secured to prevent movement during transport.
questions.explanation: Secure all cargo to keep it from moving. Loose cargo is dangerous for you and other drivers.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Is normal if a vehicle is warmed up.

questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can damage your vehicle's engine and parts.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should NOT:

options.text: Try to get out of their way.

questions.explanation: Get out of their way. Do not provoke them with eye contact or racing. Ignore rude gestures and focus on your safety.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should NOT:

options.text: Make sure your glasses are clean.

questions.explanation: Do not wear sunglasses at night. Keep your eyeglasses clean and clear. Make sure you are well-rested before driving at night.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: Warning lights turn on, then quickly turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights turn on, then quickly turn off.
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off right away after starting the engine. If they stay on, your vehicle has a problem.

questions.question: What do header boards do?

options.text: They protect drivers from being hit by cargo.
They protect drivers' heads when entering the truck cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: They protect drivers from being hit by cargo.
questions.explanation: A header board protects the driver from cargo that moves during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: How do you apply the parking brake in a newer vehicle?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, pull the yellow, diamond-shaped knob outward to apply the parking brake. Push it inward to release the brake.

questions.question: What should you do when you leave your vehicle?

options.text: Leave the keys in the ignition.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle.

questions.question: What does an over-length load require?

options.text: A convoy to stop all traffic.
A person to walk next to the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Over-length, over-width, and overweight loads require special permits. In some cases, a pilot vehicle with warning signs and flashing lights or a police escort may be needed.

questions.question: What should you check about tire wear during vehicle inspection?

options.text: The insides of the tires should be more worn than the outsides.
The outsides of the tires should be more worn than the insides.
The middles of the tires should be more worn than the outsides.
The tires should have even wear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires should have even wear.
questions.explanation: During vehicle inspection, check that tire treads are worn evenly.

questions.question: Why are ice cream trucks hazardous to other drivers?

options.text: Ice cream trucks must stay cold.
Children often run to them without looking for traffic.
Ice cream trucks leave water and ice trails on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children often run to them without looking for traffic.
questions.explanation: Ice cream trucks are hazardous because they attract children. Children often run toward them without watching for other vehicles.

questions.question: When turning quickly to avoid an object in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Apply your brakes as you steer.
Turn more than needed to miss the object.
Turn only as much as needed to miss the object.
Steer and accelerate at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only as much as needed to miss the object.
questions.explanation: When avoiding an object, turn only as much as necessary. Do not apply brakes while turning.

questions.question: What should the front of an enclosed trailer be like?
questions.explanation: When inspecting an enclosed trailer, check the front for damage such as cracks, bulges, or holes.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the safe operation of a vehicle?
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for safe vehicle operation. Always perform routine vehicle inspections before driving a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: What is the leading cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding is the leading cause of injury and death in work zones. Always slow down when driving through a work zone.

questions.question: Cargo on a flatbed trailer or trailer without sides must be:

options.text: Loose to allow it to shift when the vehicle turns.
Heavy enough that it won't shift.

questions.explanation: Cargo on a flatbed or open trailer must be securely tied down. This keeps it from shifting or falling off while you drive.

questions.question: Which surface has the least traction?
questions.explanation: Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice. Be extra careful when driving on melting ice.

questions.question: If you operate in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, which license should you get?
questions.explanation: To operate in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, you must get a non-excepted intrastate commerce license.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, how often must you check that it is secure?
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start driving, within the first 50 miles, and then every 150 miles or every 3 hours.

questions.question: To transport hazardous materials, which endorsement must you pass?
questions.explanation: You must have a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that transports hazardous materials.

questions.question: Driving at night is:

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. You cannot see hazards as well, headlight glare affects your vision, and there are more tired and impaired drivers on the road.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test, what is a pull-up?

options.text: A pull-up always counts against the applicant.
A pull-up should be completed at least once.
Stopping without changing direction is not considered a pull-up.
Excessive pull-ups are acceptable in the opinions of some test administrators.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping without changing direction is not considered a pull-up.
questions.explanation: A pull-up happens when you stop and move forward to get a better position. Just stopping is not a pull-up. Too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: What is an alcohol evaporator?

options.text: A device that adds alcohol to the air brake system to prevent freezing.
Only allowed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that adds alcohol to the air brake system to prevent freezing.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the brake system to prevent ice from forming, which can damage the brakes.

questions.question: If ice forms on your side mirror while driving, what does this mean?

options.text: The roadway is likely icy too.
The roadway will not be icy.

questions.correctAnswerText: The roadway is likely icy too.
questions.explanation: If ice forms on your mirrors or wipers while driving, the road surface is likely icy as well.

questions.question: When checking engine belts during the vehicle inspection test, what must you do?

options.text: The belts should be checked for snugness, each with up to three inches of play.
The water pump belt does not need to be identified.
The air compressor belt should be removed.
Identify which items are not belt-driven, if any.

questions.correctAnswerText: Identify which items are not belt-driven, if any.
questions.explanation: Check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts for cracks and fraying. Allow up to three-quarters of an inch of play at the center of each belt. If any of these items are not belt-driven, identify them and check that they work properly, are not damaged or leaking, and are mounted securely.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you while driving a large vehicle, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the car ahead.

questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, slow down gradually and increase your following distance. This makes it easier for the tailgater to pass. Speeding up is dangerous because the driver may continue to tailgate you at the higher speed.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the air brake tanks falls below 60 psi?

options.text: Lights flash on the outside of the vehicle.
A message appears on the control panel.

questions.explanation: When air pressure in the air tanks drops below 60 psi, a warning light will come on. On large buses, this warning may activate at 80 to 85 psi.

questions.question: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions require ____ to change gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions require double clutching to shift gears. It takes practice to do this correctly.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, a triple combination vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than ____ in one minute.
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test on a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the pressure should not drop more than 5 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: Before driving down a hill, you should:
questions.explanation: Always downshift before going down a hill. Drive at a speed that does not require constant braking.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should:

options.text: Stop soon to check that the lug nuts are tight.
Let air out of the tire to 10 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop soon to check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you change a tire, stop shortly afterward to recheck that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Shift the vehicle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Always reduce your speed and downshift before entering a curve.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should:

options.text: Never be done the same way twice.
Always be done in the same order.
Only be done on sunny days.
Not be done if the vehicle seems to be working well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be done in the same order.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you learn all the steps and makes it less likely you will forget to check something.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag can add ____ to your total stopping distance.
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your stopping distance.

questions.question: Which is not a type of retarder?
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow a vehicle and reduce braking wear. The four types are exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric.
